page: Amazon Web Services g6.8xlarge is an accelerated computing instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, targeted at graphics rendering, video processing, and machine learning inference. The compute foundation consists of an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.4 GHz, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs configured across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. System memory includes 128 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, establishing a 4 GB per vCPU distribution. Computational acceleration is delivered via a single integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU equipped with 22 GB of VRAM on the Ada Lovelace architecture. Ephemeral storage needs are met by a bundled 900 GB local NVMe SSD, complemented by 25 Gbps baseline networking.

Empirical benchmark data reveals exceptional performance in natural language processing. In large language model inference tests, the server achieves top-tier results, processing prompts at 12,203 tokens per second on 135M parameter models and 2,190.32 tokens per second on 7B models. Text generation rates reach 470.24 tokens per second and 53.34 tokens per second for 135M and 7B architectures, respectively. Single-core processing in stress-ng ranks within the top quartile at 2,990.03, while PassMark encryption scoring also shows strong competence. Geekbench image processing achieves 13,531, demonstrating solid media manipulation capabilities, though multi-core CPU evaluations and general database metrics align within mid-tier baseline averages.

The architectural profile balances dedicated CPU cores, substantial memory capacity, and hardware acceleration within a unified footprint. The inclusion of bundled 900 GB NVMe local storage reduces reliance on external volume bandwidth for scratch space and model weight caching. While the single NVIDIA L4 GPU lacks the raw memory capacity required for full-scale 70B parameter generation or large-scale distributed training, it offers high resource density for real-time inference serving. These specifications make the instance technically well suited for medium-sized LLM inference pipelines, remote graphics workstations, intelligent video analytics, automated image processing, and real-time media encoding workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services g6.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System, designed for machine learning inference and graphics-intensive tasks. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, the instance delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, supported by 128 GB of DDR4 system memory. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU with 22 GB of VRAM based on the Ada Lovelace architecture. The platform includes a direct-attached 900 GB NVMe SSD and 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations place its small and medium language model inference speeds in the top tier, matching throughput demands for real-time text processing and image manipulation. With a balanced 4 GB of memory per vCPU alongside integrated high-speed local storage, the instance presents an efficient operational profile for model deployment, video transcoding, visual rendering, and microservice-driven AI serving.
